panels.title: Headroom Tokens Saved Rate
panels.description: Tokens saved per second by headroom. The total is the compression layer (per-conversation novel savings); tool-schema deferral rides a separate attribution ledger that upstream exports with realized="false" and estimated=true, so treat that series as an estimate, not a measured saving. Sourced from headroom's /metrics via the headroom scrape job in the otelcol collector.

panels.title: Headroom Token Savings Ratio
panels.description: Fraction of billed input tokens removed by compression before the request leaves the proxy. Upstream exports no ratio histogram (no compression_ratio buckets at the pinned version), so this is derived from the saved and input counters over a 15m window.

panels.title: Headroom Latency & Overhead (avg / max)
panels.description: Overhead headroom adds to each LLM call. Upstream exports sum/count/min/max counters, not histogram buckets, so percentiles are not derivable; averages come from rate(sum)/rate(count) and the max is a since-start gauge. Compare the overhead average against the LLM Request Latency panels above to confirm headroom is a small fraction of total latency.

panels.title: Headroom Requests by Provider
panels.description: Headroom calls per second by upstream provider. Failures are 4xx/5xx excluding 429 (rate limits are counted separately below). headroom_requests_total carries no mode label at the pinned version, so the per-provider breakdown is the closest equivalent to the old mode split.

panels.title: Headroom Persistent Savings (Lifetime)
panels.description: Lifetime and current-process savings counters. Persistent counter survives proxy restarts; current counter resets when the pod rolls. The gap grows with every restart that occurs mid-conversation.

panels.title: Headroom Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Fraction of proxy requests served from headroom's own semantic cache (headroom_requests_cached_total) rather than recomputed; upstream has no headroom_cache_hits_total. High values mean headroom is reusing work; low values are expected with diverse agent traffic. Provider-side prompt caching is a different mechanism — see Headroom Provider Cache Tokens below.

panels.title: Headroom Provider Cache Tokens
panels.description: Provider prompt-cache economics per upstream provider: reads are discounted tokens, writes are billed at a premium, uncached input is full price. This is where headroom's compression savings turn into money — a high write-to-read ratio means the cache prefix keeps getting busted (see headroom_provider_cache_bust_total and headroom_cache_bust_total).

panels.title: Headroom Errors & Rate Limits
panels.description: Health signals for the proxy path: 429s split by who refused (headroom's own limiter vs. the upstream provider), exhausted-retry transport failures where the proxy answered 502 itself, and fail-open compression failures by reason (timeout vs. error). Compression failures never fail a request, but a rising rate means the compression budget is too tight or a transform is broken.

panels.title: Headroom Token Volume
panels.description: Gross billed token volume through the proxy (input prefers the provider's own usage count, falling back to a local estimate). Pair with the savings panels above to see net vs. gross traffic.

panels.title: Crawl4AI Request Rate by Handler
panels.description: Crawl4AI requests per second by route. /metrics (otelcol's 15s scrape) and /health (kubelet probes) are excluded as constant-rate noise; MCP traffic from the LiteLLM gateway shows up as /mcp/sse and /mcp/messages.

panels.title: Crawl4AI Request Rate by Status
panels.description: Crawl4AI responses per second by status code, all handlers included — a 401 on /metrics here means the otelcol bearer token no longer matches the crawl4ai startup token, and a 4xx/5xx on /mcp/* means the gateway's token or call shape is wrong.

panels.title: Crawl4AI Request Duration (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: End-to-end request latency from the FastAPI instrumentator histogram, excluding /metrics and /health as above. Buckets are the instrumentator defaults, so the p99 tail is coarse.
